title: Tekmar 671: outdoor sensor open circuit alarm
equipment: Tekmar 671 (field-derived draft; verify against the 671 manual)

n1.text: Record the exact alarm text and the Outdoor Sensor source setting. Is the control meant to use a physical outdoor sensor or Internet weather data?

r_confirm.cause: The intended outdoor source is not known, so the alarm cannot be diagnosed.
fix: Check the installation records or ask the owner or controls contractor what the outdoor source is meant to be.
Record the current setting before changing anything.

n2.text: Are the sensor terminals, cable and connections intact, and does the sensor resistance match the manufacturer chart at the measured outdoor temperature?

r_wiring.cause: Open circuit, loose or corroded connection, damaged cable or a failed sensor.
fix: Isolate the circuit as the manual directs, then check terminals, cable and the sensor for opens, shorts and moisture.
Do not infer terminals from wire colours; use the manual for this control.
Repair or replace only as the test results support, then confirm the alarm clears.

r_cfg.cause: The sensor is healthy, so the control may be configured for a different source than the one installed.
fix: Check that the Outdoor Sensor setting matches the sensor actually wired.
Record the original setting before changing it.
Confirm the alarm status and outdoor temperature after the change.

n3.text: Is the control receiving weather data? Check network connection, IP/network settings and whether the weather fields show values or dashes.

n4.text: Is the date and time set correctly on the control?

r_time.cause: Missing or incorrect time can stop the Internet weather source from updating.
fix: Set the time following the manual. If AUTO is a documented time setting, record the original setting first.
Allow the documented update interval, then check the alarm, current outdoor temperature and forecast data.
Field note: in one case, setting time to AUTO coincided with the alarm clearing and an update starting. That is a correlation, not proof of root cause; do not treat it as a universal fix.

r_net.cause: The Internet source is not delivering data.
fix: Check the network cable, router/firewall, IP configuration and the weather source settings against the manual.
Do not diagnose a physical sensor while the control is set to Internet.
Allow the update interval, then confirm data is updating.

r_verify.cause: Weather data is arriving, so the alarm may be stale or the source setting inconsistent.
fix: Check whether the alarm is active or historical and clear it only as the manual describes.
Confirm the intended source is updating and the outdoor reading is plausible against an independent measurement.
Review reset curve and WWSD settings, then verify boiler operation with the approved test procedure.
